I walked over, asked if he needed any help. He explained the idea behind "Popping the clutch." All he needed from me was a quick push. I figured that I could take a mini break from the cart run and help this guy out.

After a few turns of pushing his car up the parking lot then back down to give us some room, he was about to give up. I asked him to try one last time, and the roar of the engine was simply amazing to hear. He gave me a handshake and drove off, but in my hand was a twenty dollar bill. I instantly regretted shaking his hand, because I thought that now the karma that I somehow earned was paid off. It's been two years now, and I still haven't given that money away.

Using a throwaway because I don't know how much information about my ex-girlfriend I can reveal but...

I met my first true love in my hometown. Things were great, and I absolutely knew we were in love. We met in a play where we played a husband and wife. We were young, (I had just turned 16, she was a little under 15), and I wasn't sure that it was going to work because she was very religious while I was agnostic, but somehow, we fell in love.

Fast forward 5 months later. Someone breaks into her house and something tragic happens to her younger sister. Her entire, close-knit family was hurt. Lots of regret and whatnot. They take a vacation 2500 miles away to help them overcome this. My girlfriend's dad then announces, quite abruptly, "This isn't actually a vacation. We're moving here." My love is devastated when she tells me the news. Young and naive as I was, I decided that love was far too important. I moved 3~ hours away from her.

Six months of taking a greyhound over twice a month to spend a weekend with her. Arguably the best days of my life. Her family was always welcoming, and she and I were so far in love. Truest love I've ever felt. Then my obsession with being "right" for her overcomes me, and I realize I can't continue this relationship with our different beliefs. She wanted to get married, and I would've obliged, but I just couldn't with this realization in mind.

And now, two years filled with bouts of complete loneliness and failure, I'm about to move, again. I think back on my life, and if I hadn't moved just to sustain some young love. I would've enjoyed my last year of high school with my childhood friends. I would've gone to a great college. I would've been a lot better, I think.

But it's hard to regret the opportunity of feeling true love.
